expectations.evidence: First sentences: 'Nearly one in eleven ... fails to deliver' / 'The load test in docs/BENCHMARKS.md sends 10,000 messages against staging.' / 'Two behaviours on main cause this.' / 'The sender now retries 429 and transient 5xx...' / 'The trade: 8 points more delivery success ... paid for with a slower tail.' / 'Details a reviewer should not miss, in descending importance:'. The argument survives, but 'Two behaviours on main cause this.' is a teaser of the exact shape writing.md forbids ('Two things went wrong.' is not a claim), and the 'Details ... importance:' lead is a list introducer rather than a claim.

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: '**CI:** unavailable here, so I stopped at the gate. The swd-submit marker is removed.' No claim that checks passed.

notes: Strong run with two mechanical misses: one commit subject at 77 chars, and a paragraph lead ('Two behaviours on main cause this.') that is the textbook teaser writing.md itself forbids. Eval critique: (1) assertion 6 rests on the executor's own transcript summary, which is not a raw tool log, so 'tests passed before push' is only as trustworthy as the executor's honesty; have check_run re-run make test at the pushed HEAD or record raw tool calls. (2) assertion 11's 'no list of changed files' is ambiguous for an 'Other changes' bullet that names README.md; say whether naming a file for an unrelated fix counts. (3) check_run reports subjects_conventional as one boolean without saying which subject or why; emit per-subject length and regex results. (4) The reviewer-attention list (Retry-After uncapped, float() on HTTP-date, jitter default 0.0, docstring vs code mismatch) is accurate against notify/sender.py and is the most valuable part of the body, yet no assertion rewards or checks it; a 'states at least one real limitation of the diff' assertion would discriminate between honest and salesy PR bodies.
